signals.signal: H1-2026 Board of Directors' report (Raportul Administratorilor, 30/06/2026): 334 branches at 30/06/2026, versus 347 at 31/12/2025 and 357 at 30/06/2025 (-23 YoY). The bank says it 'further streamlined its branch network, albeit at a more moderate pace recently'.
signals.source_name: BRD BoD Report June 2026 (RO), brd.ro Investor Relations
signals.implies: Branch contraction continues but is decelerating (-13 in H1-2026 vs -23 over 12 months). Every closed unit pushes cash and routine service transactions onto machines. Printec: ATM/self-service estate expansion and redeployment, cash recyclers, managed services.
signals.likelihood: High - already occurring, continuing over 6-12 months
signals.followup: Ask BRD what happens to hardware at closed sites: redeployed to off-site lobbies or retired? That decides whether this is a new-machine sale or a logistics/managed-service sale.

signals.signal: Same report and the Q2-2026 results deck disclose that only 268 of the 334 locations offer 24H self-service capability for cash transactions - i.e. 66 units (20% of the network) have no 24/7 cash self-service zone.
signals.source_name: BRD Q2 & H1 2026 Results Presentation, slide 'A leaner, optimised network'
signals.implies: A quantified, bank-disclosed white space of 66 branch sites with no 24/7 self-service lobby. Printec: 24/7 self-service zone build-out (lobby, access control, ATM/recycler, monitoring) - a repeatable per-site package.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - self-service zone build-out is the stated substitution for branch hours
signals.followup: Obtain the 66-site list by cross-referencing the locator agency records against the 268 figure; pitch a standardised zone kit.

signals.signal: Locator harvest, 27/08/2026, via BRD's own POST endpoint /en/load/locations (filter location_to_show): 1,174 records tagged ATM (cash withdrawal, bill payment, balance, no deposit) versus 303 records tagged MBA (multifunctional ATM taking RON/EUR/USD cash deposits). Total 1,477 self-service records across 1,255 unique geo-sites. Deposit-capable share = 303/1,477 = 20.5%.
signals.implies: About 1,174 BRD self-service points are cash-out-only. This is the single largest quantified recycler/deposit-automation white space at BRD, and it replaces the dead 2021-vintage '~1,400 ATMs' boilerplate with a live, bank-published count. Printec: cash recyclers, deposit modules, cash-cycle managed services.
signals.likelihood: Medium - upgrade path is real but BRD has not announced a fleet programme
signals.followup: Re-pull the same endpoint monthly; a rising MBA count is the earliest observable signal that a recycler programme has started. Caveat: these are locator records/sites, not certified machine counts - confirm machine-per-site with BRD.

signals.signal: Same locator harvest, 27/08/2026: 335 agency records, of which 322 are classified 'cash agencies' (counter cash transactions available) and only 11 are 'cashless agencies' (multifunctional-ATM transactions only). 11 business centres.
signals.implies: 96% of BRD branches still run a manned cash desk. For comparison the Czech sector census at 01/01/2026 had only 548 of 1,426 branches with a manned cash desk. Romania is years behind on branch cash removal, so the teller-automation/recycler runway at BRD is very large and largely untouched. Printec: branch cash recyclers, teller cash automation, assisted self-service.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no announced cashless-branch programme, but headcount cuts make it structurally necessary
signals.followup: Track the 'cashless' count monthly - it moving off 11 is the trigger. Build the business case on teller FTE cost per cash desk.

signals.signal: Headcount: Bank active employees 4,641 at 30/06/2026 versus 4,965 at 31/12/2025; H1 average 4,752 versus 5,300 for 2025. Group active employees 4,798 (5,124 at 31/12/2025), H1 average 4,910 versus 5,458. Staff expenses -8.3% YoY (-10.5% YoY in Q2-2026), attributed to 'operating model optimisation through network resizing'.
signals.source_name: BRD condensed interim financial statements (Note 1) and Q2 2026 results deck
signals.implies: Staff is being removed roughly 3x faster than branches (-6.5% headcount in six months vs -3.7% branches). With 322 branches still running manned cash desks, the arithmetic forces automation of counter work. Printec: recyclers, teller automation, assisted self-service, managed services.
signals.followup: Model transactions per remaining branch FTE to size the automation gap in the pitch.

signals.signal: H1-2026 total investments RON 118m at Group level and RON 112m at Bank level, versus about RON 100m for both in H1-2025 - an increase of roughly 18% YoY. No capitalised R&D.
signals.source_name: BRD BoD Report June 2026 (RO), 'Pozitia financiara - active'
signals.implies: The investment envelope is growing but is small relative to a full self-service fleet renewal (roughly EUR 23m per half-year across everything). Printec: pitch opex/managed-service or hardware-as-a-service structures rather than a capex purchase.
signals.followup: Confirm whether the RON 118m includes leased right-of-use additions (RON 22.9m of PPE additions in H1 were right-of-use).

signals.signal: Capex mix in H1-2026 is overwhelmingly software, not hardware: intangible-asset additions RON 82.9m (FY2025: RON 186.5m), while IT and office equipment brought into service was only RON 9.1m of transfers (FY2025: RON 55.5m). Software licence expense RON 35.8m in H1-2026 vs RON 30.9m in H1-2025 (+16%). Capital commitments for intangibles rose to RON 21.4m at 30/06/2026 from RON 8.1m at 31/12/2025, against only RON 7.7m committed for tangibles.
signals.source_name: BRD condensed interim financial statements, Notes 10, 11, 32 and 36
signals.implies: BRD is currently funding software, not machines - hardware additions have collapsed to roughly one-sixth of the 2025 run-rate, and forward commitments are 2.8x larger for intangibles than for tangibles. A large recycler refresh is not currently budgeted as capex. Printec: lead with a managed-service / pay-per-transaction commercial model and with software-side content (cash forecasting, monitoring, device management) that fits the intangible budget line.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High as a purchasing-model constraint over 6-12 months
signals.followup: Watch construction-in-progress (RON 29.0m added in H1-2026) - a jump there is the leading indicator of a hardware programme being funded.

signals.signal: Cash held in tills, vaults and ATMs fell to RON 2,647.7m at 30/06/2026 from RON 2,888.4m at 31/12/2025 (-8.3% in six months), while total cash and equivalents rose 6.0% to RON 12,808m.
signals.source_name: BRD condensed separate interim financial statements, Note 3 'Numerar in casierie, tezaur si ATM'
signals.implies: Physical cash tied up in the network is shrinking faster than the network is - consistent with fewer cash desks and tighter cash management. Recycling (notes deposited are re-dispensed) is exactly the lever that cuts vault float and CIT trips further. Printec: recyclers plus cash-cycle optimisation/forecasting as a hard-ROI story measured against this balance.
signals.followup: Build the ROI case on the RON 2.65bn idle-cash balance and BRD's own CIT cost line (sundry creditors reference 'cash transportation' suppliers).

signals.signal: On 06/08/2026 BRD launched RoPay Instant payments to merchants and service providers inside the YOU BRD app, for individuals and PFA (sole traders): QR scanned from a merchant's POS terminal, static QR in-store, QR at online checkout, deep-link on mobile, and bill payment. Real-time, 24/7, RON only, no card involved, and zero commission for the payer. Infrastructure is RoPay, run by TRANSFOND with the Romanian Banking Association.
signals.source_name: BRD press release 'BRD extinde functionalitatile RoPay in YOU BRD si lanseaza platile RoPay Instant catre comercianti'
signals.implies: Account-to-account QR payment is now live at the physical POS for BRD customers. Every POS terminal in BRD's acquiring estate needs to display/accept a RoPay QR, and terminal software, reconciliation and merchant reporting all have to handle a non-card rail. Printec: POS terminal software upgrade, QR/NFC acceptance, merchant onboarding and reconciliation, plus transaction monitoring for a new instant rail.
signals.followup: Ask BRD which POS models in its estate can render a dynamic RoPay QR today and what the upgrade path is for the rest.

signals.signal: BRD's own Q2-2026 deck flags, as a NEW disclosure, 178.2 million acquiring transactions in H1-2026, alongside 97% of corporate and 96% of SME transactions digital and 80% of deposits opened in YOU BRD.
signals.source_name: BRD Q2 & H1 2026 Results Presentation, e-banking slide
signals.implies: BRD has started publishing merchant-acquiring volume, which signals that acquiring is being managed as a strategic P&L line rather than a service. Printec: POS/acquiring hardware and software, terminal estate management, value-added merchant services.
signals.followup: Get the merchant and terminal counts behind the 178.2m figure - BRD does not publish them.

signals.entity: Romania - Fiscal Procedure Code / RoPay scheme
signals.signal: Law no. 239 of 15/12/2025 amended Law 207/2015 (Fiscal Procedure Code) to widen the definition of 'modern payment means' to include app-based digital solutions that initiate an account-to-account payment order, alongside debit, credit and prepaid cards. RoPay is presented by the scheme operator as satisfying that definition.
signals.implies: Romanian merchants subject to the electronic-acceptance obligation can now satisfy it with a QR code instead of a card POS terminal. This is simultaneously a threat to card-POS unit volumes and an opening for QR-capable terminals and softPOS. Printec: POS/acquiring product strategy for Romania must cover A2A QR, not only card.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - already in force, adoption ramping through 2026
signals.followup: Read the full text of Law 239/2025 to confirm exactly which merchant categories the acceptance obligation binds and whether a QR alone discharges it.

signals.signal: RoPay's participant list shows BRD live with six payment types (QR Friend, QR at POS/checkout, displayed QR, invoice QR, e-commerce QR on desktop, e-commerce deep-link on mobile). CEC Bank, Libra, ING, BCR, Banca Transilvania, Salt Bank, VISTA and UniCredit are also live with broad feature sets; Raiffeisen is live only with alias (phone-number) payments; BRCI is shown as in implementation. CEC Bank, Libra and VISTA offer feature sets at least as wide as BRD's, and VISTA additionally lists NFC contactless RoPay.
signals.implies: A2A QR acceptance is becoming table stakes across the Romanian market, not a BRD differentiator, which raises the pressure on merchant-side acceptance infrastructure at every acquirer. Printec: multi-bank POS/QR acceptance offering, terminal software, merchant onboarding.
signals.followup: Check the RoPay 'participanti acceptatori' page for which acquirers/processors can actually onboard merchants - that is the commercial gate.

signals.signal: In Q2-2026 BRD strengthened its digital onboarding by enabling the new Romanian Electronic Identity Card (CEI) with chip for remote customer identification and application activation, and added State Treasury payments with mandatory fiscal fields inside YOU BRD.
signals.source_name: BRD 2026 Half-Year Report / BoD Report June 2026
signals.implies: BRD has committed to chip-eID-based remote identification. That same chip-read capability is what upgrades in-branch and self-service onboarding (eID reading at an assisted kiosk or ATM). Printec: digital onboarding/eKYC, eID document reading, identity verification at the self-service point.
signals.followup: Ask whether CEI chip reading is mobile-NFC only or whether BRD wants it at branch/self-service devices too.

signals.signal: BRD published a customer warning on 04/08/2026 about a phishing campaign impersonating the bank under the pretext of 'confirming an incoming payment', driving victims to a fake YOU BRD page that harvests credentials and authorises further transactions.
signals.implies: Credential-phishing plus authorised-push-payment abuse against a bank that has just opened an instant, irrevocable A2A merchant rail (RoPay). That combination is exactly the risk profile that drives behavioural transaction-monitoring and real-time fraud scoring spend. Printec: transaction monitoring, fraud detection, AML/compliance.
signals.followup: Check whether BRD has issued further phishing notices and whether ANPC/BNR has commented on instant-payment fraud in Romania.

signals.signal: BRD's published 'Program decalat' list shows 25 named units operating on shifted hours, 24 of them with a compulsory midday closure of 30 minutes (e.g. 13.00-13.30 or 12.30-13.00). Locations span Bucharest, Brasov, Timisoara, Baia Mare, Targu Jiu, Bistrita, Deva, Reghin, Aiud, Ineu, Pancota, Viseu de Sus and others.
signals.implies: Staffing is thin enough at 25 units that the counter simply shuts at lunchtime - a concrete, named service gap that a 24/7 self-service zone or a recycler closes. Printec: targeted per-site self-service zone pitch using BRD's own list.
signals.followup: Cross-reference these 25 named units against the locator MBA list to find which have no deposit machine - the sharpest possible target list.

signals.signal: Current report 34/2026 dated 22/07/2026: Safetech signed a significant contract worth EUR 2,728,000 excluding VAT, 36 months, for cybersecurity services, sale of its own cybersecurity monitoring solution and sale of other security solutions. The beneficiary is explicitly stated as CONFIDENTIAL - 'entitate din Romania neafiliata Companiei' (a Romanian entity not affiliated with the company). Safetech also reported H1-2026 consolidated net profit of RON 8.5m, +53% YoY, and a 48-month framework agreement with the Authority for the Digitalisation of Romania.
signals.implies: NO BRD LINK IS CONFIRMED - the counterparty is undisclosed and nothing in BRD's or Safetech's public filings names the other. Reported here because the Safetech angle was tasked and the honest answer is that it does not currently attach to BRD. Standing relevance: a domestic SOC/monitoring vendor is winning multi-year Romanian contracts at this scale, which is the competitive backdrop for any Printec AML/transaction-monitoring or managed-security pitch in Romania.
signals.likelihood: Low as a BRD-specific event; High as market context
signals.followup: If the BRD-Safetech hypothesis matters, the only routes are Safetech's annual report client concentration disclosure or a direct market check - it cannot be resolved from the 22/07/2026 filing.

coverage_notes: Fresh run, no checkpoint existed. Primary-source route: BRD H1-2026 Board of Directors' report (RO), the EN Half-Year Report and the RO semiannual filing on BVB infocont, the Q2/H1-2026 results presentation from brd.ro IR, and the 14/08/2026 current report (auditor review only, no new operational content). PDFs were pulled and text-extracted locally with pdfminer. Second angle: BRD's own branch/ATM locator, driven directly through its POST endpoint /en/load/locations with the location_to_show filter, giving fresh 27/08/2026 counts (1,174 ATM / 303 MBA / 335 agency / 322 cash / 11 cashless / 11 business / 1,255 unique sites) - this is the replacement for the dead 2021 '~1,400 ATMs' figure. Third angle: BRD's own sitemap lastmod dates were mined to surface August 2026 press items that no search would have ranked, which produced the 06/08/2026 RoPay Instant merchant launch and the 04/08/2026 phishing notice. Fourth angle, new source environment: the RoPay scheme site (TRANSFOND/ARB), which yielded the participant map and the Law 239/15.12.2025 amendment to the Fiscal Procedure Code. Baseline re-verification: 334 branches / 347 at Dec-25 / 357 at Jun-25 and RON 118m Group / 112m Bank H1-2026 investment are all CONFIRMED against the primary BoD report, and the H1-2025 comparative (~RON 100m) is added. The dead '~1,400 ATMs / ~1,600 terminals' figure was NOT carried. GAPS: (a) BRD publishes no machine count, POS terminal count or merchant count anywhere - the locator figures are site/record counts, not certified machine counts, and are flagged as such; (b) no evidence of any BRD recycler procurement, tender or vendor announcement exists in public sources - the recycler case here is inferred from the deposit-capability gap, not from a disclosed programme, and I have not asserted otherwise; (c) the Safetech-BRD link asked for in the brief does not exist in public filings - the July 2026 contract counterparty is explicitly confidential; (d) BNR national ATM/POS statistics were not obtained (see access issues), so BRD's estate is not benchmarked against the Romanian market total this run; (e) WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted after two queries, so everything after that point was reached by direct fetch, sitemap mining and endpoint probing rather than search.
access_issues: bvb.ro PDF downloads time out on curl (connection timeout at 90s, repeatedly); route used was WebFetch, which saves the binary locally, then local pdfminer extraction - logged rather than dropped. brd.ro/sites/default/files/2024-12/Agentii_inchise_3.pdf ('Temporarily closed BRD branches') returns an HTML 404 page with a .pdf extension - the closed-branch list is therefore unavailable and the sibling Program_decalat.pdf was used instead. brd.ro/en/press-releases, /comunicate-de-presa, /en/news all 404; the press index had to be reconstructed from https://www.brd.ro/sitemap.xml lastmod dates. bnro.ro 302-redirects to bnr.ro; bnr.ro/1947-statistica-plati and /2151-plati return only navigation chrome to the fetch tool, with the actual datasets sitting behind the 'Baza de date interactiva' JS application - not resolved this run, no press substitute used. brd.ro locator returns no data in HTML; resolved by reading the Drupal footer bundle (delta=1), recovering mapGeneralSettings.loadLocationsUrl and calling the POST endpoint directly - no Chrome escalation was needed. transfond.ro/ro/ropay/ returns only navigation; ropay.ro was used instead.
operator_requests: 1) Full text of Law no. 239/15.12.2025 amending Law 207/2015 (Fiscal Procedure Code) from Monitorul Oficial - needed to establish precisely which merchant categories the electronic-acceptance obligation binds and whether a RoPay QR alone discharges it without a card POS. This is the single most commercially material open question for Printec's Romanian POS business. 2) BNR payment-system statistics (ATMs, POS terminals, cards) for 2025 and H1-2026 from the BNR interactive database - the JS application blocks the fetch tool, and these figures are needed to benchmark BRD's 1,477 self-service records and its 178.2m acquiring transactions against the national totals.
